1.  Use the `PimaIndiansDiabetes` dataset. Use 15% data for testing. Use cross-validation with of 7 folds to tune random forest `(method='ranger')`. What are the parameters that produce the greatest accuracy? What is the testing accuracy.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(mlbench)
library(ranger)

data(PimaIndiansDiabetes, package = "mlbench")
df <- tibble(PimaIndiansDiabetes)
df$diabetes <- as.factor(df$diabetes)

# split
set.seed(123)
splitIndex <- createDataPartition(df$diabetes, p = 0.85, list = FALSE)

df_train <- df[splitIndex, ]
df_test <- df[-splitIndex, ]

# folds
trControl <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 7)

# tune
tuneGrid <- expand.grid(mtry = 2:4, splitrule = c("gini", "extratrees"),
                        min.node.size = 1:10)

set.seed(123)
forest_ranger <- train(diabetes ~ ., data = df_train, method = "ranger",
                       trControl = trControl, tuneGrid = tuneGrid, metric = "Accuracy")

print(forest_ranger)
```

2. Use the `PimaIndiansDiabetes` dataset. Go to https://topepo.github.io/caret/available-models.html and pick a classification model.  Tune the classification model using cross-validation of 7 folds. 

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(mlbench)
library(rpart)

data(PimaIndiansDiabetes, package = "mlbench")

df <- tibble(PimaIndiansDiabetes)
df$diabetes <- as.factor(df$diabetes)

# split
set.seed(123)
splitIndex <- createDataPartition(df$diabetes, p = 0.85, list = FALSE)

df_train <- df[splitIndex, ]
df_test <- df[-splitIndex, ]

# folds
trControl <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 7)

# tune
tuneGrid <- expand.grid(maxdepth = 2:10)

set.seed(123)
tree_model <- train(diabetes ~ ., data = df_train, method = "rpart2",
trControl = trControl, tuneGrid = tuneGrid, metric = "Accuracy")

print(tree_model)

# besth
tree_model$bestTune

plot(tree_model)
```

3. (Model Comparison) Use the `PimaIndiansDiabetes` dataset. Pick two models at [this link](https://topepo.github.io/caret/available-models.html) to compare using 7-fold cross validation method. Evaluate the accuracy of the final model on the test data.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(mlbench)
library(rpart)
library(ranger)

data(PimaIndiansDiabetes, package = "mlbench")

df <- tibble(PimaIndiansDiabetes)
df$diabetes <- as.factor(df$diabetes)

# split
set.seed(123)
splitIndex <- createDataPartition(df$diabetes, p = 0.85, list = FALSE)

df_train <- df[splitIndex, ]
df_test <- df[-splitIndex, ]

# folds
trControl <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 7)

# decision tree
set.seed(123)
tree_model <- train(diabetes ~ ., data = df_train, method = "rpart2",
trControl = trControl, tuneGrid = expand.grid(maxdepth = 2:10),
metric = "Accuracy")

# random forest
set.seed(123)
forest_model <- train(diabetes ~ ., data = df_train, method = "ranger",
trControl = trControl, metric = "Accuracy")

# compare
results <- resamples(list("Decision Tree" = tree_model,          "Random Forest" = forest_model))

bwplot(results)

summary(results)

# compare
tree_accuracy <- max(tree_model$results$Accuracy)
forest_accuracy <- max(forest_model$results$Accuracy)

comparison <- data.frame(Model = c("Decision Tree", "Random Forest"),
Cross_Validation_Accuracy = c(tree_accuracy, forest_accuracy))

print(comparison)

# select higher
if (tree_accuracy >= forest_accuracy) {final_model <- tree_model
final_model_name <- "Decision Tree"} else {final_model <- forest_model
final_model_name <- "Random Forest"}

cat("Selected final model:", final_model_name, "\n")

# eval
pred <- predict(final_model, df_test)

cm <- confusionMatrix(data = pred, reference = df_test$diabetes)

cat("Testing accuracy:", cm$overall["Accuracy"], "\n")

print(cm)
```
